description:
## Why

Where the BEAM already has a native answer (:erlang.crc32, :binary.match, String.valid?, :crypto, crc32cer's hardware CRC32C) defk loses or ties: those are hand-tuned C/assembly with SIMD and hardware instructions, while defk emits plain checked C and relies on clang's auto-vectoriser. Today that works for simple loops (ws_masking ~38 GB/s, scale 16 elements per iteration), helped by strips, branch-free check flags and replay (defk-6tt, defk-hki). Two things limit it: build.ex sets no -march (fine on arm64, where NEON is baseline; SSE2-only on x86-64), and the subset has no way to express hardware instructions or SIMD algorithms (shuffles, lane masks).

This epic researches and prototypes closing that gap without giving up what defk is for.

## Constraints (non-negotiable)

- Elixir mode stays an exact oracle: every new builtin or type has an Elixir implementation and agreement properties.
- Memory safety: no read or write outside an array, including vector loads at the tail.
- Float results stay bit-exact with Elixir (-ffp-contract=off, no reassociation; check that any -march flag doesn't change this, e.g. FMA, denormal modes).
- Kernels still read as Elixir. Raw per-architecture intrinsics (_mm256_*, NEON) in kernel source are out of scope: non-portable, unemulatable at scale, unsafe loads.
- Honest benchmarking: every number says which target it was built for; an architecture build is compared with the best Elixir and with the portable build.

## The central choice: build for portability or build for architecture

Likely outcome: the user chooses. A portable build (today's default) runs on any machine of the OS/arch; an architecture build (-march=native or a named level such as x86-64-v3 / armv8.2-a+crc) is faster but only runs on CPUs with those features. The epic must answer:

- API and devex: where the choice is made (config :defk, a use Defk option, an env var for CI, per kernel?), what the default is, how it reads in mix.exs/config, how a user learns whether it helped (report: :full vectorisation remarks), and what happens on a wrong CPU (a clear error at load naming the missing features, or a fallback; never SIGILL).
- Deploys: mix release built on one machine and run on another (CI vs prod, Docker buildx multi-arch, mixed fleets); whether one release can carry several variants and pick at load (runtime dispatch, target_clones / function multiversioning); cache key and .so naming; interaction with shipping .so files in releases (defk-n8f) and with the C-compiler stance (examples/release_debian).

## Children

Research first (vectorisation headroom, target levels), then prototypes (opt-in target flag with load-time check, deploy variants, hardware builtins, a vector-type ceiling study), then the decisions (target API, vector types), then devex validation of whatever is chosen.

Done when the decisions are recorded with measurements from real arm64 and x86-64 hardware, and the chosen target API is implemented, documented and cold-tested (or the epic records why not).
